title: Why Kylian Mbappe has been cancelled in China
description:
Kylian Mbappé - the French football superstar sometimes nicknamed a ‘Dictator’ online - has found himself at the centre of a scandal in China this week, after mentioning one of the memes made about him. It shows his face on the body of Mao Zedong, the former Chinese leader, and on a French talk show, when Mbappé describes it, he refers to Mao as a dictator.

The backlash against Mbappé has been huge. He’s been dropped by major Chinese brands, shops have pulled football shirts with his name off the shelves, and the state broadcaster has even stopped showing La Liga matches. Mbappé, Real Madrid and La Liga - the Spanish league - have all apologised.

So how did a joke about meme become so controversial in China - and what does it tell us about censorship in the country? Kerry Allen, the BBC’s China Media Analyst, talks us through it all - and we hear from the BBC Global China Unit’s Shawn Yuan, who explains how censorship in China is changing.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討法國足球巨星 Kylian Mbappé 因談論將自己臉部合成至毛澤東身上的迷因並稱其為獨裁者，而在中國遭到全面抵制的事件。事件導致多個中國品牌終止合作、球衣下架，央視亦暫停轉播皇家馬德里的西甲賽事。雖然 Mbappé 與西甲均已致歉，但中國官媒仍嚴格審查相關細節。節目亦探討了中國日益嚴格且不可預測的審查制度，以及年輕球迷在官方抵制與對體育明星喜愛之間的矛盾心理。
summaryEn: This episode explores why French football superstar Kylian Mbappé was cancelled in China after discussing a meme showing his face on Mao Zedong's body and referring to Mao as a dictator on a French talk show. Following the incident, major Chinese brands terminated sponsorships, merchandise was removed from store shelves, and state broadcaster CCTV stopped showing Real Madrid's La Liga matches. Despite apologies from Mbappé, Real Madrid, and La Liga, Chinese state media continue to censor the specifics of the controversy. The episode also examines China's increasingly strict and unpredictable censorship climate, past sports and celebrity boycotts, and how young Chinese fans navigate official cancel culture when it targets international sports icons.
